title: Write a GLSL MAT
summary: Official Derivative guide for GLSL materials, including GLSL 3.30+ shader stages, TD transform/deform helpers, custom geometry and POP attribute access, lighting/shadow/projection APIs, camera/stage defines, multi-camera instancing rules, picking support, multiple render targets, and Render TOP image-output helpers.
guidance: Use this article when a plan needs custom GLSL MAT vertex/pixel shader source, POP/SOP attribute access in materials, or Render TOP image-output shader helpers.

Treat older online or WebGL examples as migration starting points only: current TouchDesigner GLSL MAT code uses GLSL 3.30+ conventions, TouchDesigner supplies the #version statement, and legacy built-ins such as gl_FragColor need current output declarations.
Default vertex transforms should use TDWorldToProj(TDDeform(TDPos())) unless the material intentionally overrides deformation.
Declare custom or POP-compatible attributes on the GLSL MAT Attributes page before using TDAttrib_AttribName().
Use TDTexAttrib_AttribName(textureLayer) when shader code should read POP attributes and SOP texture coordinates through the same path.

Use the Buffers page and TDBuffer_AttribName(elementIndex, arrayIndex) when arbitrary POP attributes must be accessed by element index; pair it with TDBufferLength_AttribName() and cTDBufferArraySize_AttribName for bounds and array-size logic.

Use TD_NUM_LIGHTS, TD_NUM_ENV_LIGHTS, TD_NUM_CAMERAS, and shader-stage defines such as TD_VERTEX_SHADER, TD_PIXEL_SHADER, and TD_COMPUTE_SHADER when writing shared DATs or loops that must recompile cleanly for changing render contexts.

Use TDLightingPBR(), TDEnvLightingPBR(), or TDLighting() for material lighting paths and reach for the lower-level shadow and projection helpers such as TDHardShadow(), TDSoftShadow(), TDProjMap(), TDShadowTexture(), and TDProjTexture() only when custom light math is required.
Use TDDeformNorm(TDNormal()) for normals and TDDeform/TDDeformVec for positions or vectors because TouchDesigner returns these deformed values in World space, not model/SOP space.

For skinning deforms, avoid names reserved by the GLSL MAT Deform feature and remember SOP pCapt/pCaptPath/pCaptData inputs map to POP BoneIndices and BoneWeights; direct helpers such as TDSkinnedDeform() and TDBoneMat() are usually lower-level than TDDeform().
Use TDInstanceID() instead of gl_InstanceID or uTDInstanceIDOffset, and use TDCameraIndex() or TDTrueCameraIndex() for multi-camera Render TOP workflows.

When an instance id or TDInstanceTextureIndex() result must reach the pixel shader, pass it as a flat varying such as flat out int vInstanceID or flat uint; integer instance values must not be interpolated.
For instance texturing, fetch TDInstanceTextureIndex() for the current instance and sample TDInstanceTexture() in the shader stage that owns the chosen index.
Call TDCheckDiscard() near the start of the pixel shader when order-independent transparency, dual-paraboloid rendering, or other discard-aware features might be active.
Call TDCheckOrderIndTrans() at the start of the pixel shader when Order Independent Transparency should be supported; it is safe when OIT is disabled in the Render TOP.
Use TDPointCoord() instead of gl_PointCoord for point sprites so coordinates match TouchDesigner orientation expectations.

Use TDFrontFacing(), TDFog(), TDDither(), TDPixelColor(), and TDOutputSwizzle() near the pixel-output path when front/back-facing tests, camera fog, Render TOP dithering, Geo Text glyph rendering, or output channel swizzling matter.

For Render Pick DAT/CHOP support, guard shader paths with TD_PICKING_ACTIVE, call TDWritePickingValues(), then override vTDPickVert or vTDCustomPickVert fields only after that call when custom vertex positions or custom pick attributes are needed.
Pass material color outputs through TDOutputSwizzle and call TDAlphaTest when alpha testing is needed.

For multiple Render TOP color buffers, declare outputs against TD_NUM_COLOR_BUFFERS, inspect results through Render Select TOP, and avoid writing past the configured buffer count because that can corrupt output or crash the GPU.

For Render TOP image outputs, call TDImageStore_Name() and TDImageLoad_Name() under TD_RENDER_TOP guarded code; TouchDesigner declares the images when the MAT is compiled for the Render TOP, so shader code should not declare the image uniforms itself.
Use Specialization Constants with layout(constant_id = 0) for rarely changing shader modes or switches; they cache specialized shader variants and should not be used for constantly changing values.
Use #include to share DAT shader code by absolute or relative path while still letting TouchDesigner supply the GLSL #version statement automatically.
